allies.rationale_text: First-principles-thinking helps jobs-to-be-done strip away the familiar solution and recover the underlying need that actually matters.
allies.source_quote: JTBD operates like a form of arguing from first principles.
allies.affinity_rationale: JTBD 'operates like a form of arguing from first principles' — requires stripping away conventional assumptions to get back to the basic, undeniable need.
allies.activation_condition: When identifying the true customer job requires decomposing past the product category and conventional market assumptions to the fundamental need being served

allies.rationale_text: Critical-thinking supports jobs-to-be-done by repeatedly questioning whether the team has identified the real job or only a convenient surface explanation.
allies.affinity_rationale: JTBD is described as 'inherently dependent on critical thinking' — requires constantly asking 'why, why, why?' to uncover the root cause and ensure the identified job is correct.
allies.activation_condition: When the initially stated customer need may be a symptom rather than the root job, requiring disciplined interrogation to reach the true underlying motivation

allies.rationale_text: Systems-thinking helps jobs-to-be-done connect the identified user purpose to the broader machine that must deliver that outcome.
allies.source_quote: structure the rest of the business or product as a machine
allies.affinity_rationale: JTBD 'helps structure the rest of the business as a machine designed to achieve that specific goal' — the job provides the telos that organizes system design.
allies.activation_condition: When the identified job needs to be translated into an organizational or product system designed around delivering that specific outcome

allies.rationale_text: Feynman-technique supports jobs-to-be-done by forcing the job definition into plain language before the team commits to a solution story.
allies.source_quote: Mitigation often relies on metacognition and using structured processes, like the Feynman Technique, to simplify the complex job definition into plain language.
allies.affinity_rationale: Positioned as a practical tool to 'simplify the complex job definition into plain language and use analogies to fill knowledge gaps' — ensures deep understanding of the core job.
allies.activation_condition: When the job definition has become complex or abstract and needs to be pressure-tested through plain-language explanation to verify genuine understanding

antagonists.rationale_text: Confirmation-bias corrupts jobs-to-be-done when the team defines the job to fit a preferred solution instead of pressure-testing what the user is really hiring for.
antagonists.source_quote: Identifying the Job based on a desired conclusion or a pre-selected solution, rather than objective reality.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Identifying the 'Job' based on a desired conclusion or a pre-selected solution rather than objective reality — directly corrupts the discovery process that JTBD demands.
antagonists.activation_condition: When the job definition is framed to confirm an existing product hypothesis rather than discovered through genuine observation of user behavior and motivations

structured_tensions.tension_text: Jobs-to-be-done conflicts with confirmation-bias when the job definition is framed to confirm an existing product hypothesis rather than discovered from user evidence.
structured_tensions.source_quote: jobs-to-be-done conflicts with confirmation-bias (confirmation bias) when the job definition is framed to confirm an existing product hypothesis rather than discovered from user evidence.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Jobs-to-be-done conflicts with simplification when reducing customer needs to a single job erases the multi-dimensional trade-offs that actually drive choice.
structured_tensions.source_quote: jobs-to-be-done conflicts with simplification (simplification) when reducing customer needs to a single job erases the multi-dimensional trade-offs that actually drive choice.
